back: Discrete: counted, only particular values (number of goats). Continuous: measured, any value in a range (mass, time).
Primary: collected by the investigator for the purpose. Secondary: collected by someone else (records, reports).
Splits each value into a stem and a leaf; leaves in order; keeps every raw value; always needs a key.
Two data sets share one stem; left leaves increase away from the stem (read right to left). Key explains both sides, e.g. $3 \mid 13 \mid 5$.
Minimum, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, maximum — the five values a box plot shows.
Outlier if below $Q_1 - 1.5(Q_3 - Q_1)$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5(Q_3 - Q_1)$. Whiskers stop at the most extreme non-outliers.
Positive skew: median nearer $Q_1$, longer upper whisker. Negative skew: median nearer $Q_3$, longer lower whisker.
Quote one measure of location (median) and one of spread (IQR), with values, and interpret each in context.
